newsitem.title: USA: United Carolina soars on surprise merger.
newsitem.headline: United Carolina soars on surprise merger.

text.p: United Carolina Bancshares Corp soared on news of a surprise deal for the bank to be acquired by Southern National Corp in a $985 million stock transaction.
United Carolina was up 9-1/2 to 37 in early trading.

"This illustrates a shift in their acquisition strategy," said John Bailey, analyst at Friedman, Billings, Ramsey. He said for the last year Winston-Salem, N.C.-based Southern National has been expanding into neighboring Virgina. The deal with Whiteville, N.C.-based United Carolina Bancshares represents an in-market merger, he noted.

Bailey noted that while the announcement was a surprise, the stock of United Carolina Bancshares has been strong lately. He noted the stock advanced more than five percent from mid-October to the end of October. United Carolina jumped 1-1/2 to 27-1/2 Friday, a rise of more than five percent.

United Carolina shareholders will receive 1.135 shares of Souther National for each United Carolina share, valuing the shares at $40.01 based on Friday's closing price of $35.25 per share for Southern National.
Southern National declined 1-3/8 to 33-7/8 in early dealings Monday.
